\section{Introduction}\label{sec:intro}
A live preview must answer a keystroke faster than the reader can notice.
The usual approach --- recompile the whole document on every change --- is
correct but slow, and it also loses the reader's place on the page. These
notes describe the two mechanisms that avoid both problems: a block cache
keyed by source bytes, and a page builder that replays TeX's cost model.

We assume familiarity with the standard \LaTeX{} document model: a preamble,
a sequence of sectioning commands, paragraphs, display material and floats.
Nothing here depends on a particular class; the examples use
\texttt{article} because it is the class of most of the corpus.
